text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites, and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are good at tasks like answering questions, summarizing texts, and translating languages. However, they also have limits. They can make mistakes, sometimes produce false information, and do not truly understand meaning. Despite these weaknesses, LLMs are powerful tools that are changing how we work and communicate.
